canonical_data: specs, task requirement files, context manifests, and per-developer journals under the repository's .trellis directory
current_repo_note: The root LICENSE is the plain AGPL-3.0 text and the CLI manifest declares AGPL-3.0-only, but the COPYRIGHT file says "or any later version"; the narrower reading is recorded.
strengths: Keeps the workflow's state in the repository itself, with task directories, curated context manifests, and journals that the next session reads back
A PreToolUse hook rewrites the sub-agent call to inject the task's context, so the injection is enforced by code rather than left to the prompt
One structure works across 22 coding platforms, and an ablate and restore pair removes and recovers every managed file from a verified backup
weaknesses: It configures and steers host agents rather than executing work, so task outcomes still depend on whichever coding agent runs
AGPL-3.0 on an engineering workflow that lives inside a company repository is a licensing question a reader has to settle
The license text, the manifest, and the COPYRIGHT header disagree on "only" versus "or later"
why_it_matters: Shows a workflow layer that owns durable project state and injects it by hook into whichever coding agent a team already uses.
